papers.title: Latest $ν$s from the Earliest Galaxies: Probing neutrino self-interactions with JWST
papers.authors: Ranjini Mondol, Priyank Parashari, Anirban Das, Vera Gluscevic, Ranjan Laha
papers.abstract: Our Universe serves as a complementary laboratory for particle physics interactions. One intriguing possibility is that neutrinos may have beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) self-interactions, which can delay their free streaming and have an observable effect across different redshifts. Such interactions can induce scale-dependent changes in the matter power spectrum. The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has opened up a new window onto the early Universe by discovering a large population of high-redshift galaxies up to $z \sim 15$ and various probable galaxy candidates at even higher redshifts, between $z \sim 15-30$. Such high-redshift observations can probe the matter power spectrum on small scales, since structure formation is hierarchical and the structures hosting these high-redshift galaxies are therefore expected to be small. We, $\textit{for the first time}$, use the UV luminosity function data from JWST and combine them with the $\textit{Planck}$ CMB data to probe neutrino self-interactions ($\nu$SI). If only one neutrino flavor experiences such BSM interactions, then $\textit{Planck}$ + JWST data give a 95% C.L. upper limit on $\mathrm{Log}_{10}(G_{\mathrm{eff}}/\mathrm{MeV}^{-2})$ $\approx$ $-2.75$ and when all three flavors are interacting, the corresponding constraint becomes $\lesssim -3.41$; both stronger than those obtained using only $\textit{Planck}$ data. Our results highlight the power of this new observable, the high-redshift UV luminosity function from JWST as a complementary probe to terrestrial experiments, showing that small-scale observables can open a new window onto smaller neutrino self-interaction strengths.

papers.title: Breaking dark degeneracies in $k$-essence models with redshift-space distortions
papers.authors: Rebecca Briffa, Lehel Csillag, Erik Jensko
papers.abstract: Dynamical dark energy models are often difficult to constrain with background observations alone due to parameter degeneracies. This is especially true when the dark energy sector evolves through an effective pressureless matter phase, leading to degeneracies between the model parameters and the matter density parameter. In this work, we show that redshift-space distortion (RSD) measurements help break this degeneracy when combined with expansion history probes including Pantheon$^{+}$ supernovae and DESI DR2 BAO measurements. We demonstrate this in the ghost and dilatonic ghost condensate $k$-essence models, restricting the observational analysis to physically admissible solutions by imposing the absence of ghosts and gradient instabilities. Given the small scalar sound speeds in these models, we also explicitly check the validity of the quasi-static approximation used in the growth analysis. Our results show that combining growth-rate data with stability requirements and standard background observations provides a fast and efficient way to constrain potentially degenerate dark sector models. Lastly, we discuss the matter clustering constraints on these models in light of the recent $S_8$ discrepancies.

To address this, the authors test whether redshift-space distortion (RSD) growth-rate measurements ($f\sigma_8$) can break these degeneracies in two kinetic scalar field models: the ghost condensate and the dilatonic ghost condensate $k$-essence models. Using MCMC sampling with observational data from Pantheon+ supernovae, DESI DR2 BAO, cosmic chronometers, and RSD growth rates, they enforce physical stability priors to strictly exclude ghosts ($Q_s > 0$) and Laplacian/gradient instabilities ($c_s^2 \ge 0$). Additionally, because $k$-essence fields can have very small sound speeds ($c_s^2 \to 0$), the authors quantitatively verify that the quasi-static approximation remains valid on linear RSD scales due to background suppression of dark energy perturbations.
conclusions: Enforcing non-ghost ($Q_s > 0$) and gradient stability ($c_s^2 \ge 0$) theoretical priors restricts the scalar field to stable non-phantom evolution ($-1 \le w_\phi < 1/3$) and subluminal propagation speeds ($0 \le c_s^2 < 1/3$).

RSD growth-rate measurements ($f\sigma_8$) significantly break the background parameter degeneracy between $\Omega_{m,0}$ and dark energy parameters, proving especially crucial for the dilatonic ghost condensate model.

The quasi-static approximation for matter perturbations remains valid on linear RSD scales ($k \sim 0.01 - 0.02 \, h\text{Mpc}^{-1}$) despite vanishingly small scalar sound speeds, as dark energy density perturbations remain strongly suppressed by $\Omega_\phi(1+w_\phi) \ll 1$.

Both ghost condensate models prefer slightly higher central values for the clustering amplitude $S_8$ than $\Lambda$CDM, though model selection metrics (BIC) still favor standard $\Lambda$CDM due to its fewer free parameters.

papers.title: Viable Phantom Crossing in Softly Broken Shift Symmetric Gravity
papers.authors: Rodrigo Calderon, Eric V. Linder
papers.abstract: We demonstrate a viable fit to current cosmological data from a simple Horndeski modified gravity theory that softly breaks shift symmetry. This SBSS model crosses the phantom divide $w=-1$ at $z\approx0.5$ and fits observational data (baryon acoustic oscillations and supernova distances, and cosmic microwave background power spectra) better than $w_0w_a$CDM, by $\Delta\chi^2\approx-3$ for the same number of effective parameters, while providing a physical foundation for cosmic acceleration. The theory is healthy, has no cosmological constant or potential, and has substantial protection against high energy quantum loop corrections.

The authors propose 'Softly Broken Shift Symmetric' (SBSS) gravity within luminal Horndeski theory, where shift symmetry holds at high energies to protect against quantum corrections but is softly broken at late times via exponential field modulations in the kinetic ($K$) and braiding ($G_3$) terms. They analyze the autonomous dynamical system, show that the model naturally transitions through $w = -1$ while remaining stable and ghost-free, and fit the background cosmology to DESI DR2, Union3.1 supernovae, and Planck 2018 CMB data.
conclusions: SBSS gravity provides a healthy, ghost-free physical mechanism for crossing the phantom divide around $z \approx 0.5$ without requiring a potential or cosmological constant.

Fitting DESI DR2 BAO, Union3.1 SNe, and Planck 2018 CMB yields an improvement of $\Delta\chi^2 \approx -3$ and a log Bayes factor preference $\Delta\ln Z \approx +3.1$ relative to $w_0w_a$CDM for the same number of effective dark energy parameters ($N_\mathrm{par} = 2$).

Because the theory maintains minimal tensor coupling, gravitational slip remains unity ($\eta = 1$), but kinetic braiding generates a time-dependent $G_\mathrm{eff}(z)$ that predicts testable deviations in linear structure growth.

papers.title: Algebraic classification of single-field inflationary dynamics
papers.authors: Jinn-Ouk Gong, Wei-Chen Lin
papers.abstract: We develop an algebraic classification of canonical single-field inflationary dynamics using an exact depressed cubic equation for the inflaton velocity. Its root structure identifies a branch-swap boundary distinct from the limiting boundary of downhill motion, where ultra-slow-roll inflation naturally emerges. Independently, the conservation of momentum conjugate to the comoving curvature perturbation in the long-wavelength limit provides a criterion for the growth or decay of the gauge-invariant difference between comoving and uniform-density curvature perturbations. Combining these criteria, we construct a unified dynamical chart in terms of the Hubble and potential slow-roll parameters, illustrating its applicability to constant-roll inflation and simple toy models. Our classification shifts the emphasis from assigning models to fixed categories toward understanding the dynamical regimes traversed by inflationary trajectories and their implications for primordial perturbations.

The authors develop an exact algebraic framework for canonical single-field background dynamics by expressing the inflaton velocity as a depressed cubic equation. From its root structure, they identify an algebraic branch-swap boundary as well as a strict physical bound for downhill inflaton motion ($\\eta > -6 + 2\\epsilon$). Independently, using the conserved momentum conjugate to the comoving curvature perturbation $\\mathcal{R}$ on super-horizon scales, they formulate a physical criterion for the growth of the gauge-invariant curvature difference $|\\zeta - \\mathcal{R}|$. Combining these criteria yields a unified dynamical chart in slow-roll parameter space, allowing one to map out the dynamical trajectory of an inflationary model across different background and perturbation regimes.
conclusions: The inflaton velocity satisfies an exact depressed cubic equation, whose discriminant structure reveals a branch-swap boundary at $\\eta_{\\text{swap}} = -6(1-\\epsilon)$ where physical trajectories switch between lower- and higher-velocity algebraic branches.
Monotonic downhill inflaton motion requires $\\eta > -6 + 2\\epsilon$, establishing ultra-slow-roll (USR) on a flat potential as the limiting boundary of maximally damped downhill kinetics.

Super-horizon growth of the gauge-invariant curvature difference $|\\zeta - \\mathcal{R}|$ is dictated by $\\Gamma_{\\mathcal{R}} = 3 - \\epsilon + \\eta < 0$, which is physically and dynamically distinct from both the background branch-swap boundary and the USR limit.

The authors construct a 2D dynamical chart in $(\\epsilon, \\chi)$ space to trace inflationary trajectories, demonstrating that curvature perturbation growth can begin well before entering higher-velocity or USR regimes.

papers.title: Confirming HSC strong lens candidates with DESI Spectroscopy. II. Analysis of 80 galaxy-scale systems with lens redshifts above 0.8
papers.authors: Shen Li, Yiping Shu, Lin Nie
papers.abstract: The total mass distribution of galaxies provides a sensitive probe of the fundamental physical processes governing galaxy evolution, including gas inflow/star formation, AGN/SN feedback, galaxy merging, and the nature of dark matter. State-of-the-art cosmological simulations have therefore made extensive predictions for the evolution of the total-mass density slope. Interestingly, their predictions diverge significantly at high redshift, primarily due to differences in how these key physical mechanisms are implemented. However, measurements of the total-mass structure evolution have been largely confined to low and intermediate redshifts, leaving the regime where model predictions differ most significantly (z>0.8) largely unexplored. In the first paper of this series, we reported the discovery of 84 candidate strong-lens systems with lens redshifts above 0.8. In this work, we perform lens modeling of the 80 galaxy-scale systems to assess their lensing nature. Of these, 71 systems (approximately 90%) exhibit clear lensing features that are well reproduced by our lens models and are therefore classified as secure strong lenses. Another eight systems are classified as probable (5) or possible (3) strong lenses, based on the prominence of their lensing features and the quality of the lens modeling. One system lacking reliable lensing features in current imaging data is classified as a non-lens. Our analysis nearly triples the number of known galaxy-scale strong lenses at z_lens > 0.8, making statistical studies of the total mass structure of high-redshift galaxies possible for the first time. This expanded sample provides an unprecedented opportunity to test the predictions of cosmological simulations and discriminate between competing physical prescriptions.

In this paper, the authors conduct parametric gravitational lens modeling using five-band ($grizy$) Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) imaging for 80 high-redshift candidate galaxy-scale lenses identified from Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR1 spectroscopy. Using Singular Isothermal Ellipsoid (SIE) mass models plus external shear in `lenstronomy`, combined with PPXF full-spectrum fitting for stellar kinematics and CIGALE SED modeling for stellar masses, they evaluate the physical properties and lensing nature of each system. They securely confirm 71 strong lens systems (roughly 90% of the sample), 5 probable lenses, and 3 possible lenses, while identifying 1 non-lens. This work nearly triples the existing sample of known galaxy-scale strong lenses at $z_{\rm lens} > 0.8$, establishing a large high-redshift dataset to test sub-grid physical prescriptions in cosmological simulations.
conclusions: Joint five-band modeling confirms 71 secure strong lenses out of 80 high-redshift ($z_{\rm lens} > 0.8$) candidates, along with 5 probable lenses, 3 possible lenses, and 1 non-lens.
Measured central stellar velocity dispersions from DESI spectra range from $91$ to $515\text{ km s}^{-1}$ with a median of $232\text{ km s}^{-1}$ and a median fractional uncertainty of $14.9\%$.
SED fitting yields lens galaxy stellar masses spanning $\log_{10}(M_\star/M_\odot) = 9.08\text{--}12.10$ (median $11.36$) and a median main stellar population age of $4.52\text{ Gyr}$.
At fixed stellar mass, early-type lens galaxies at $z_{\rm lens} > 0.8$ exhibit smaller rest-frame $5000\text{ \AA}$ effective radii on average than lower-redshift lens samples.
A total of 56 systems (70% of the sample) lie within scheduled footprints for space-based imaging surveys including Euclid, CSST, or Roman.

papers.title: Probing the Seed Effect of Supermassive Primordial Black Holes with Weak Gravitational Lensing
papers.authors: Lei Zu, Kazunori Kohri
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmological implications of supermassive primordial black holes (PBHs) as a component of dark matter (DM), focusing on their seed effect on large-scale structure formation. In contrast to the Poisson effect associated with the discrete distribution of PBHs, the seed effect arises because PBHs act as early gravitational seeds, accreting surrounding DM and developing dense DM spikes to form dressed PBHs. These structures enhance the matter power spectrum, particularly on small scales. We model their contribution within the halo-model framework under two prescriptions for DM accretion: an optimistic scenario (Case 1) and a conservative scenario (Case 2), which predict different modifications to the 1-halo term. We constrain the PBH abundance using weak-lensing measurements from the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 (DES Y3), performing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis to derive upper limits on the PBH fraction $f_{\rm PBH}$, as a function of the PBH mass $M_{\rm PBH}$. We find that weak lensing places competitive constraints on supermassive PBHs, with the upper limits on $f_{\rm PBH}$ becoming progressively stronger toward higher PBH masses. Case 1, which predicts more efficient DM accretion and hence a larger enhancement of the matter power spectrum, yields stronger constraints than Case 2; in particular, it excludes $f_{\rm PBH}\gtrsim10^{-4}$ for $M_{\rm PBH}\gtrsim10^{10} M_\odot$. We further forecast the sensitivity of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) using mock weak-lensing data and find that the constraints could improve by approximately two orders of magnitude. Our results establish weak gravitational lensing as a sensitive probe of the seed effect of supermassive PBHs and demonstrate its potential to complement other cosmological and astrophysical searches.

papers.title: Comment on the recent claims of H0 measurements with the ZTF DR2 SN Ia sample (arXiv:2610.36051)
papers.authors: Mickael Rigault, Brodie Popovic, Ariel Goobar, Suhail Dhawan, Marie Aubert, Marc Betoule, Umut Burgaz, Georgios Dimitriadis, Lluís Galbany, Tomás E. Müller Bravo, Antoine Gilles Lordet, Madeleine Ginolin, Young-Lo Kim, Marek Kowalski, Jakob Nordin, Nicolas Regnault, Mathew Smith, Jesper Sollerman, Jacco H. Terwel, Alice Townsend
papers.abstract: Karchev et al. (2026) derived a value of H0 by combining the ZTF SN Ia DR2 sample with SH0ES calibrator Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia; Riess et al. 2022), used to anchor the SN Ia absolute luminosity. The ZTF SN Ia DR2 dataset (Rigault et al., 2025) is the largest (O(3000)) SN Ia sample to date obtained with a single telescope. However, as emphasized in the data release, the absolute photometric calibration of the survey has not yet been established to the precision required for cosmological inference. The relative photometric zeropoint offset between the SH0ES and ZTF SN Ia DR2 samples, which is fully degenerate with H0, is therefore unknown and cannot be determined from publicly available data. The photometric corrections introduced in Karchev et al. (2026) do not address this global calibration offset. Consequently, their reported H0 determination is not supported by the available calibration information. We nonetheless share the excitement of pursuing state-of-the-art cosmology with ZTF and are actively working toward the release of a fully calibrated dataset

ai.summary: Local measurements of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) using Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) rely on anchoring distant Hubble-flow SNe to nearby calibrator SNe on a unified photometric zero-point scale. Recently, Karchev et al. (2026) claimed an independent determination of $H_0$ by combining the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) DR2 SN Ia dataset with SH0ES calibrators. In this comment, members of the ZTF collaboration clarify that the public ZTF DR2 lightcurves lack absolute photometric zero-point calibration relative to external systems (such as Pan-STARRS/SH0ES) and contain uncorrected instrument non-linearities (e.g., CCD 'pocket effects' and filter bandpass variations). Because a zero-point offset $\Delta(\text{mag})$ directly biases $H_0$ via $\Delta H_0 / H_0 = -(\ln 10 / 5) \Delta(\text{mag})$, the authors conclude that Karchev et al.'s reported $H_0$ value and tension with Planck are unsupported by the public dataset.
conclusions: The $H_0$ measurement reported by Karchev et al. (2026) using ZTF DR2 and SH0ES is invalid due to an unconstrained global photometric zero-point offset between the two datasets.

A calibration offset of 0.05 mag biases $H_0$ by $\approx 1.7\text{ km s}^{-1}\text{Mpc}^{-1}$; potential uncalibrated offsets in ZTF DR2 could reach 0.1 mag (a $\sim 3.5\text{ km s}^{-1}\text{Mpc}^{-1}$ systematic shift).

Uncorrected detector non-linearities (such as the CCD 'pocket effect' and forced-photometry versus scene-modeling photometry shifts of $\sim 60\text{ mmag}$) cannot be corrected post hoc without access to raw stellar magnitude data products.
ZTF DR2 remains valid for internal relative studies (e.g., SNe Ia population properties), but robust cosmological constraints require the forthcoming fully calibrated ZTF data release.

papers.title: GradFlex: a Gradient-Based Method for Weak Lensing Flexion Measurement
papers.authors: Jiarui Sun, Jun Zhang, Toshifumi Futamase
papers.abstract: Flexion, the second-order gravitational lensing distortion, probes small-scale mass distribution and complement the cosmic shear measurement. However, its detection is highly challenging due to the faint signal and the contamination arising from the intrinsic galaxy morphology. In this Letter, we present GradFlex, a new method that extracts flexion from the gradient field of galaxy surface brightness distributions without assuming a specific point-spread function model or galaxy morphology. Using surface-brightness conservation, we relate the pre- and post-lensing gradient fields and derive flexion estimators from ensemble-averaged statistics of the corresponding spins. Tests on numerical simulations across diverse galaxy morphologies and multiple noise realizations demonstrate its reliability under realistic observing conditions. Combined with shear measurements, it could tighten constraints on cluster density profiles and enable more detailed studies of substructure than shear alone.

ai.summary: Gravitational lensing flexion represents the second-order spatial gradient of weak lensing convergence and shear, probing small-scale mass variations like subhalos in galaxy clusters. Detecting flexion from galaxy images is notoriously difficult due to faint signals, point spread function (PSF) convolution, noise, and complex galaxy morphologies. The authors present GradFlex, a gradient-based method that extracts first (spin-1) and second (spin-3) flexion from surface brightness gradient fields in Fourier space without assuming a specific PSF model or parametric light profile. Using surface brightness conservation and ensemble-averaged spin statistics with derived response factors, the method isolates flexion signals from galaxy shape noise. Tests on simulated regular (Sérsic) and irregular galaxies demonstrate that GradFlex recovers reduced flexion accurately in the weak-distortion regime and remains stable against noise and centroiding uncertainties.
conclusions: GradFlex provides a model-independent estimator for reduced flexion ($F$ and $G$) based on ensemble averages of surface brightness gradient products in Fourier space.

Simulation tests confirm accurate signal recovery in the weak-lensing regime, though systematic biases occur near halo centers where higher-order terms like shear-flexion couplings become non-negligible.
The method demonstrates strong resilience against background noise down to $\text{SNR} \sim 20$ when paired with a Friends-of-Friends based circular masking approach.
Centroid shifts between the brightest pixel and flux-weighted center cause minimal impact (under $2\%$ change for regular galaxies) on the extracted flexion.

papers.title: Multi-Probe Cosmological Constraints on Clustering DBI Dark Energy Scenario
papers.authors: Samit Ganguly, Surhud More, Goutam Manna, Kazuharu Bamba, Eduardo Guendelman, Abhijit Bhattacharyya
papers.abstract: We present a multi-probe observational analysis of a clustering tachyonic Dirac-Born-Infeld~(DBI) dark energy model. Its noncanonical kinetic term gives a subluminal sound speed, so dark energy perturbations can grow on subhorizon scales. Working in a multifluid framework that tracks both the background expansion and linear perturbations, we constrain the model with nested sampling, using Planck 2018 compressed CMB distance priors, DESI DR2 BAO, cosmic chronometers, $f\sigma_8$ growth data, and three Type Ia supernova compilations: Pantheon$+$, DES-SN5YR, and Union3. The standard cosmological parameters agree with $\Lambda$CDM within $2\sigma$, with DBI preferring a slightly lower $H_0$ and higher $\Omega_{m0}$, with the largest shift being $\simeq1.8\sigma$ in $H_0$ for Pantheon$+$. The Bayesian evidence favours DBI in every compilation, moderately for Pantheon$+$ ($\Delta\ln\mathcal{Z}\simeq3.4$) and inconclusively for DES-SN5YR and Union3 ($\Delta\ln\mathcal{Z}\simeq0.6$-$0.7$). The field thaws naturally. Dark energy perturbations stay several orders of magnitude below matter perturbations, yet the noncanonical sound speed still alters the Hubble friction term, raising $S_8$ by only $\approx0.5\sigma$ relative to $\Lambda$CDM. Four independent diagnostics, namely the CPL parametrization, $Om(z)$, the statefinder hierarchy, and the growth index, all point to genuinely evolving dark energy rather than a cosmological constant. The thermal history is left intact, with negligible early dark energy. However, one limitation remains. Because $w_\phi=\dot\phi^2-1\geq-1$, the phantom regime is out of reach, which is in line with the no-go theorem for a single minimally coupled scalar field, so the model cannot follow the DESI DR2 preference for an effective equation of state crossing $w=-1$.

papers.title: The box within the Universe: anisotropies in periodic cosmological simulations I. Dark-matter-only simulations
papers.authors: Gábor Rácz, Till Sawala
papers.abstract: The vast majority of cosmological simulations employ periodic boundary conditions to achieve statistical homogeneity and to mimic the infinite spatial extent of our Universe. In a cubic periodic domain the Green function breaks full rotational invariance and introduces a geometry-induced anisotropy in the gravitational interaction. We quantify how this intrinsic anisotropy affects cosmic structure growth and investigate the extent to which it biases the commonly used large-scale structure and halo-based observables in dark-matter-only simulations. We analyse an ensemble of 498 cosmological dark-matter-only $N$-body simulations in cubic $T^3$ topological manifolds, evolved to $z=0$, spanning box sizes from $L=6.25\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ to $L=100\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ at fixed mass and force resolution. We compare anisotropy-sensitive statistics across the suite, including the matter power spectrum, halo abundance, merger histories, shapes and alignments, and filament orientations. Finite periodic boundaries imprint orientation-dependent signatures aligned with the box geometry. These signatures propagate beyond the largest modes and can induce systematic shifts in both field-level and halo-level statistics. The detectable effects propagate to scales much smaller than the box size. Our results demonstrate that periodic-box anisotropy is a non-negligible source of systematics for small simulation volumes, including those commonly employed in modern hydrodynamical simulations.

However, this topology breaks continuous $SO(3)$ rotational symmetry down to the discrete octahedral point group $O_h$, introducing an intrinsic, box-aligned gravitational force anisotropy that invalidates total angular momentum conservation. In this paper, the authors evaluate an ensemble of 498 dark-matter-only simulations with box sizes ranging from $L=6.25\text{ Mpc}$ to $100\text{ Mpc}$ at fixed mass and force resolution to quantify how these boundary artifacts distort cosmological statistics. They demonstrate that geometry-induced anisotropic tidal fields couple through non-linear evolution, propagating directional biases to scales much smaller than the box size and corrupting halo abundances, shapes, alignments, and filament orientations in small periodic volumes.
conclusions: Cubic periodic boundary conditions ($T^3$ topology) reduce full continuous rotational symmetry to the discrete octahedral group $O_h$, leading to non-conservation of total angular momentum due to net torques from periodic images.

Non-linear mode coupling propagates the box-aligned anisotropic gravitational tidal field down to small physical scales, systematically biasing halo shapes, alignments, merger histories, and filament orientations.
Small periodic boxes ($L \lesssim 25\text{ Mpc}$), commonly used in modern hydrodynamical galaxy-formation runs, suffer from significant macro-environment orientation biases at late times ($z=0$).

To suppress periodic-box anisotropy effects below the percent level at $z=0$, standalone simulations require box sizes of $L \ge 100\text{ Mpc}$, or should employ cosmological zoom-in techniques inside a large parent volume.

papers.title: Joint analysis of the Macquart relation and the dispersion measure power spectrum: cross-covariance and redshift self-calibration
papers.authors: Amy Wayland, Robert Reischke
papers.abstract: The dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace ionised baryons along the line of sight, probing baryonic feedback. Two complementary observables can be constructed from an FRB catalogue: the DM-redshift (Macquart) relation of host-identified FRBs, and the angular power spectrum of the DM field of the full catalogue. Their joint analysis requires their cross-covariance. We derive it within the halo model and show it is a super-sample effect: only the monopole of an individual DM correlates with the angular power spectrum, yielding an exact, model-independent bound on the correlation coefficient. We validate the calculation against log-normal forward simulations of $10^4$ FRBs. For individual DMs, the correlation with the bandpowers is at the per cent level. Neglecting the cross-covariance changes the width of the $\chi^2$ distribution by only 0.8 per cent, so the two observables can be treated as effectively independent for wide-area surveys. In a joint forecast with an LSST-like weak lensing survey, adding the Macquart relation tightens constraints on the physical baryon density by 32 per cent and on the mean host contribution by a factor of 4.1, while improving baryonification parameters by only about 5 per cent, indirectly through the host contribution. Finally, we show that the redshift distribution of FRBs without identified hosts, which enters every DM power spectrum, can be reconstructed by inverting their DMs with the jointly fitted mean relation without biasing the inferred parameters, whereas a 20 per cent error in the mean relation biases the DM power spectrum by up to 2$\sigma$ per band for $5\times 10^5$ FRBs.

papers.title: A multi-epoch VLBI study of compact symmetric objects as contaminants in the search for milli-lenses
papers.authors: Diego Álvarez-Ortega, Felix M. Pötzl, Carolina Casadio
papers.abstract: The Lambda Cold Dark Matter model predicts a high abundance of low-mass dark matter halos, which can be probed through milliarcsecond-scale gravitational lensing (milli-lensing) of background radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGNs). The Search for MIlli-LEnses (SMILE) project aims to find these rare systems with Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI). However, compact symmetric objects (CSOs) can closely resemble milli-lenses in VLBI images and are the main contaminant in such searches. We aim to determine the nature of the nine remaining milli-lens candidates of the SMILE pilot study and to characterize their physical properties. We analyzed all available multi-epoch, multi-frequency archival VLBI data, new HSA and EVN observations, and single-dish and connected-element interferometer measurements. We tested the lensing hypothesis through the morphology and spectra of the sources, and characterized their kinematics, spatially resolved spectral indices, magnetic fields, and integrated spectra, using synchrotron self-absorption (SSA) and free-free absorption (FFA) models. We identify eight of the nine candidates as CSOs, four of them for the first time. Spectral index asymmetries between components and previously undetected emission connecting them rule out the lensing hypothesis. Only J0923-3435 remains ambiguous. For the CSOs with known redshifts, the lobes have equipartition magnetic fields of $\sim$20-320 mG and projected separations of $\sim$60-240 pc, and show no measurable expansion, implying kinematic ages of at least $\sim$50-950 yr. The integrated spectra of J0210-2213 and J2347-1856 favor an inhomogeneous external free-free absorber over homogeneous and inhomogeneous SSA models. Since CSOs will be the main contaminant in the full SMILE survey, applying this framework will provide the same constraints for a much larger sample of compact radio-loud AGNs.

papers.title: Scalar perturbations in two-scalar-field warm inflation
papers.authors: Orlando Luongo, Tommaso Mengoni, Paulo M. Sá
papers.abstract: We investigate scalar perturbations in a two-scalar-field cosmological model unifying warm inflation, dark matter, and dark energy. The inflaton is noncanonically coupled to a second scalar field that acts as dark energy at late times. Assuming negligible dissipation and perturbations of the dark-energy field, we derive the linear scalar perturbations in a gauge-ready form, including quantum and thermal noise in the inflaton sector and stochastic fluctuations of the energy transfer to radiation. We numerically solve the coupled perturbation system using a Fokker-Planck formalism and compute the scalar spectral index $n_s$ and the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ for dissipation coefficients scaling as $T^p$ with $p=-1,\, 1$ and $3$. For $p=-1$, we find scenarios compatible with current CMB observations in both the weak and strong dissipative regimes, while the explored scenarios with $p=1$ and $3$ are outside the observationally supported regions. Compared with standard single-field warm inflation, the two-scalar-field model yields a systematically larger spectral index for a given tensor-to-scalar ratio.

For a benchmark point, we find a first-order phase transition and compute the resulting gravitational wave (GW) spectrum, which we compare with the projected sensitivities of space-based interferometers. Although the viable parameter space is small, it can be probed by future experiments.

papers.title: Thorium and Europium production in the early Galaxy: Implications for nucleocosmochronology
papers.authors: L. Magrini, R. E. Giribaldi, M. Palla, S. Randich, L. Pasquini, C. J. Hansen, R. Smiljanic, M. Racca, M. Tsantaki, J. Schiappacasse-Ulloa, A. Skuladottir, G. Kordopatis, L. Berni, T. Matsuno, G. Casali, V. Hill, F. Matteucci, G. Cescutti, F. Rizzuti, E. Spitoni

Combining these measurements with homogeneous literature samples, we investigate the behaviour of log(Th/Eu) as a function of metallicity. The derived ages are consistent with expectations for an old, metal-poor halo population, although individual uncertainties remain substantial. Higher spectral resolution is needed to improve Th measurements, while combining stars in coeval populations can provide additional statistical gains. Homogeneous samples of coeval stars, particularly in globular clusters, observed with future high-resolution multi-object spectrographs could provide stronger constraints on the early formation history of the Milky Way and the age of the Universe.

papers.abstract: Type II Cepheids (T2Cs) are Population II pulsating stars that serve as distance indicators through their period--luminosity relation. Along with RR Lyrae stars and the tip of the red giant branch, they offer an independent route to the Hubble constant, helping assess systematic uncertainties in its determination. We aim to investigate the impact of chemical composition on T2Cs' period--luminosity relations by building a homogeneous spectroscopic sample of Galactic T2Cs with iron and oxygen abundances. We observed 80 Galactic T2Cs with UVES at the ESO Very Large Telescope. For 74 stars, we derived stellar parameters and iron and oxygen abundances through a self-consistent spectroscopic analysis based on equivalent widths of absorption lines. This sample nearly doubles the number of T2Cs with spectroscopic metallicity measurements available in the literature. We used these abundances to test theoretical predictions for the instability strip and, together with $Gaia$ parallaxes, to derive Period--Wesenheit--metallicity (PWZ) relations. In agreement with theoretical predictions, the metallicity coefficient ($\gamma$) is small and statistically consistent with zero in all relations, ranging from approximately $-0.02$ to $+0.17$ mag dex$^{-1}$. We also estimated distances to 22 Galactic Globular Clusters hosting T2Cs, finding agreement within uncertainties with independent literature estimates. Our results show that metallicity has, at most, a minor impact on T2Cs' pulsation properties and distance scale, supporting their reliability as Population II distance indicators.

papers.title: Long lived MeV scale bound state dark matter alleviates the ${}^7 Li$ tension
papers.authors: Pa. Gokhula Prasad, V. Suryanarayana Mummidi
papers.abstract: We investigate the impact of MeV scale unstable bound state dark matter on both thermal and non thermal Big Bang nucleosynthesis. Focusing on the weakly self interacting regime, we find that this framework can reproduce the theoretically predicted abundances through both short and long lived bound states. While long lived bound states can alleviate the cosmological ${}^7$Li problem, they simultaneously lead to discrepancies with other light element abundances. We show that this tension is resolved by incorporating non thermal nucleosynthesis, which act on these non standard initial light element abundances to alleviate the ${}^7 Li$ tension without violating observational constraints on the other elements. Remarkably, across the range of $\widetilde{\rho}_B$ and $m_\chi$ considered, long lived bound states with lifetimes $10^0\,{\rm s}\lesssim\tau\lesssim10^2\,{\rm s}$ can simultaneously resolve the ${}^7$Li problem and a large parameter space remain consistent with the observed abundances of the other light elements. Our results demonstrate that non thermal effects are essential for obtaining a consistent nucleosynthesis history in unstable bound state dark matter scenarios.

By combining thermal nucleosynthesis with late-time non-thermal photodisintegration effects, the authors demonstrate that these dark sector decays can effectively deplete ${}^7$Li to observed levels. papers.title: Can $n_s$ hint at a parity-odd sector of gravity?
papers.authors: Christian Dioguardi
papers.abstract: We study slow-roll inflation in the context of metric-affine gravity. We consider the most general projectively invariant metric-affine theory at most quadratic in the distortion and linear in curvature with no propagating torsion and non-metricity and couple it non-minimally to a scalar field. We focus on the class of $\xi$-attractors, in which a single function $f(\phi)$ fixes the whole scalar sector. Integrating out the non-dynamical distortion generates a correction to the kinetic term $k(\phi)$ which is $f'(\phi)^2$ times a ratio of polynomials in $f(\phi)$. The new kinetic term can develop poles at finite field values, where the distortion field equations degenerate. We classify the poles and derive the conditions on the effective couplings for poles of order $p=2$ and $p=3$, the maximal order allowed in this setting. We then proceed to study inflation. Second-order poles realize $\alpha$-attractors with $\alpha$ fixed by the residue and are already available in the parity-even sector of the theory. Third-order poles instead require the parity-odd sector: whenever the parity-odd quadratic couplings vanish, the kinetic function splits into two independent terms with poles of order at most $p=2$. Third-order pole-inflation, as we confirm numerically for $f(\phi)\propto\phi^2$, yields $r\propto N_*^{-3/2}$ with a tunable amplitude and $n_s\simeq 1-\tfrac{3}{2N_*}$, a spectral index mildly larger than the $\alpha$-attractor prediction and well centered in the region preferred by the current combination of ACT, SPT and DESI data. Moreover, when inflation happens far away from the pole we also find a further universal attractor, an inverse-linear plateau, with $n_s \simeq 1-\frac{4}{3N_*}$ and $r\propto N_*^{-4/3}$, testable with the forthcoming BICEP/Keck observations.

papers.title: Torsion talks only to spin: the CMB temperature as a test of energy exchange in Einstein-Cartan cosmology
papers.authors: Fernando Izaurieta, Samuel Lepe, Cristian Quinzacara
papers.abstract: The cosmic microwave background temperature at $z=0.886$ is known to $2\%$ from molecular absorption towards PKS~1830$-$211; CO absorbers and Sunyaev-Zel'dovich clusters extend the measurement to $z\simeq3$. We use them on a question that cosmologies with torsion leave open. When the geometry exchanges energy with several matter components, which of them receives it? In Einstein-Cartan theory the Noether identities of each sector fix the answer. A sector's energy-momentum fails to be conserved only in proportion to its own spin, so minimally coupled light, which has none, is conserved whatever the torsion does. A metric-affine cosmology fitted to DESI DR2 distributes the exchange ``universally'' among all fluids, radiation included; the photons then gain almost a third of their energy. If the photons stay a blackbody, as FIRAS requires of any source set by local conditions, the model predicts a background colder than $T_{0}(1+z)$ by $7\%$ at $z\simeq0.9$ and by $8.5\%$ at $z\gtrsim3$, with no free parameter. PKS~1830$-$211 gives $5.08\pm0.10\,\mathrm{K}$ against a predicted $4.78\,\mathrm{K}$; with the CO absorbers it favours the standard scaling by $\Delta\chi^{2}=13$, and 18 Planck cluster bins give $\chi^{2}=50.8$ versus $15.5$. Under the same reading the primary anisotropies would change their spectral shape by amounts Planck excludes. If dark matter carries the spin instead, $H(z)$ moves by less than $10^{-4}$ below $z=3$ at the fitted parameters and $T(z)$ is standard again.

papers.title: Searching for axion-like particles with SPHEREx
papers.authors: Marco Regis, Marco Taoso, Jorge Terol Calvo
papers.abstract: We study prospects to detect axion-like particles (ALPs) with the upcoming near-infrared telescope SPHEREx. The signal under investigation is the ALP decay into two photons. Assuming dark matter (DM) to be in the form of ALPs, we analyze the signal from the DM halos of dwarf spheroidal galaxies, the Large Magellanic Cloud and the Milky Way. We find that SPHEREx can significantly improve current limits on the axion-photon coupling in the 0.5-3 eV ALP mass range.

papers.title: Are magnetic fields in cosmic voids primordial?
papers.authors: Deepen Lark, Ruth Durrer, Jennifer Schober
papers.abstract: The existence and origin of magnetic fields in cosmic voids remains an open question: Observational evidence inferred from gamma-ray spectra of TeV blazars has been debated for over a decade, while early-Universe magnetogenesis models typically invoke physics beyond the Standard Model of particle physics. We propose a late-Universe contribution to void fields from the dipole components of galactic magnetic fields. In the conducting intergalactic medium, these fields spread through turbulent magnetic diffusion, and the galaxies residing within voids reduce the required propagation distance to a few Mpc, a scale bracketed by current estimates of the turbulent diffusivity. In the regime where the propagation distance is sufficient, the superposition of randomly oriented galactic dipoles produces volume-filling void fields with a white-noise spectrum and amplitudes well above the lower bounds inferred from the absence of GeV halos around TeV blazars. These fields constitute an astrophysical background that must be accounted for before void fields are interpreted as relics of primordial magnetogenesis, and they could account for the void fields without requiring primordial fields at all. Their white-noise spectrum provides a distinctive observational signature.

papers.title: Dark Energy Crosses the Line: Quantifying and Testing the Evidence for Phantom Crossing
papers.authors: Emre Özülker, Eleonora Di Valentino, William Giarè
papers.abstract: Combinations of the most recent CMB, BAO, and SNeIa datasets, when analyzed using the CPL parametrization, $w(a) = w_0 + (1 - a) w_a$, exclude $\Lambda$CDM at $\gtrsim\!3\sigma$ in favor of a dark energy equation of state (EoS) parameter that crosses the phantom divide. We confirm this behavior and show that it persists when DESI BAO data are replaced by SH0ES $H_0$ measurements, despite the known tension between these probes in the presence of CMB data. In both cases, the constraints favor a transition from an early-time phantom-like phase to a late-time quintessence-like phase, with the crossing occurring at different redshifts depending on the dataset combination. The probability that a phantom divide line (PDL) crossing does not occur within the expansion history is excluded at significance levels ranging \mbox{between $3.1\sigma$\,--\,$5.2\sigma$.} To investigate whether the apparent PDL crossing is a genuine feature preferred by the data or an artifact of the linear form of the CPL parametrization, we isolate the PDL crossing feature by introducing two modified versions of CPL that explicitly forbid it: CPL${}_{>a_\mathrm{c}}$ and CPL${}_{<a_\mathrm{c}}$. These models are physically motivated in that they phenomenologically capture the behavior of thawing and freezing scalar field scenarios. While previous studies have primarily considered thawing quintessence as a non-crossing alternative, we find that a freezing phantom-like model is the only one capable of performing comparably to CPL--and only in a few cases. Nevertheless, across all dataset combinations considered, the standard CPL model consistently provides the best fit, strongly indicating that the data genuinely favor a PDL crossing.

papers.title: Constraints on Compact Dark Matter Population from Micro-lensing Effect of Gravitational Wave for the third-generation gravitational Wave Detector
papers.authors: Xin-Yi Lin, Xi-Jing Wang, Huan Zhou, Zhengxiang Li
papers.abstract: Since the first direct detection of gravitational waves (GWs) from a binary black-hole merger by the LIGO-Virgo Collaboration, GWs have emerged as a powerful probe of astrophysics and cosmology. If extragalactic compact dark matter (DM) candidates, such as primordial black holes, constitute a non-negligible fraction of the DM component over a broad mass range, they can imprint distinctive microlensing signatures on GW signals. In this work, we develop a framework to infer the population properties of extragalactic compact DM by simulating microlensing GWs in the frequency band of the third-generation ground-based GW detector, the Einstein Telescope, and analyzing them via hierarchical Bayesian inference. For a population described by a power-law mass function, we show that the detection of only several microlensing GW events among $10^4$ binary black-hole coalescences can constrain the compact DMs abundance to the level of $\sim 10^{-3}$. This forecast demonstrates that searching for and identifying microlensing signatures in future GW observations can provide a complementary approach to constraining compact DM scenarios.

papers.title: Clustering redshift distribution calibration of weak lensing surveys using the DESI-DR1 spectroscopic dataset
papers.authors: R. Ruggeri, C. Blake, J. Aguilar, S. Ahlen, D. Bianchi, D. Brooks, F. J. Castander, T. Claybaugh, A. Cuceu, K. S. Dawson, A. de la Macorra, B. Dey, P. Doel, A. Elliott, N. Emas, S. Howlett, D. Huterer, M. Ishak, S. Joudaki, R. Joyce, D. Kirkby, A. Krolewski, O. Lahav, C. Lamman, M. Landriau, J. U. Lange, A. Leauthaud, M. E. Levi, M. Manera, A. Meisner, R. Miquel, J. Seo, J. Silber, D. Sprayberry, G. Tarlé, B. A. Weaver, P. Zarrouk, R. Zhou, H. Zou
papers.abstract: We estimate the source redshift distribution of current weak lensing surveys by applying the clustering-based redshift calibration technique, using the galaxy redshift sample provided by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 1 (DESI-DR1). We cross-correlate the Bright Galaxy Survey (BGS), Luminous Red Galaxies (LRGs) and Emission Line Galaxies (ELGs) from DESI, within the redshift range $0.1 < z < 1.6$, with overlapping tomographic source samples from the Dark Energy Survey (DES), Kilo-Degree Survey (KiDS), and Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) survey. Using realistic mock catalogues, we test the stability of the clustering redshift signal to fitting scale, reference-sample choice, and the evolution of source galaxy bias. We calibrate a source galaxy bias correction from simulations with conservative (factor-of-two inflated) priors to account for modelling uncertainties, and we explicitly model and marginalise over magnification contributions, which become non-negligible at $z \gtrsim 1$ due to the depth of the DESI ELG sample. We then compare the resulting bias-weighted redshift distributions to \rossi{previously calibrated redshift distributions from the literature, based on self-organising map (SOM) techniques}, finding agreement within uncertainties for all surveys and tomographic bins. Our results demonstrate that clustering redshifts enabled by DESI's unprecedented spectroscopic sample provides a robust, complementary, and independent constraint capable of reducing one of the dominant systematic uncertainties in weak lensing cosmology.

papers.title: Searching for Cosmological Collider in the Planck CMB Data II: collider templates and Modal analysis
papers.authors: Petar Suman, Dong-Gang Wang, Wuhyun Sohn, James R. Fergusson, E.P.S. Shellard
papers.abstract: Signatures of massive particles during inflation are highly informative targets for cosmological experiments. With recent progress on both theoretical and observational frontiers, we have reached the point where these novel signals of primordial non-Gaussianities (PNG) can be systematically tested with increasingly precise data. In this paper, we present the results of improved CMB data analysis for cosmological collider signals using Planck CMB data. To set the stage, we first construct a set of simplified but characteristic collider templates which are accurate over a broad range of particle masses, spins and sound speeds. In order to break degeneracies with single-field PNG, we propose an orthogonalization scheme such that the collider templates are uncorrelated with the highly constrained equilateral and orthogonal shapes. On this basis, we deploy the Modal bispectrum estimator for the Planck analysis and perform a systematic scan of parameters to search for the most significant collider signal. The maximum signal-to-noise ratio is found to be $2.35\sigma$ for an orthogonalized massive spin-0 exchange after taking into account the look-elsewhere effect. In addition, we cross-validate the Modal analysis with the CMB-BEST pipeline, which demonstrates the consistency of results across the benchmark examples of collider templates. Given the low signal-to-noise ratio regime we find at the current stage of PNG observations, we believe the orthogonalization procedure provides an optimized strategy for future tests of the cosmological collider signals.

papers.title: Spectral Hierarchy of the Cosmic Web
papers.authors: Francisco-Shu Kitaura, Francesco Sinigaglia
papers.abstract: We introduce a spectral hierarchy of cosmic-web classifications obtained by applying simple scale-weighting kernels to the density field before performing a standard eigenvalue-based web classification. This unifies and extends several widely used web definitions within a single framework: the familiar potential/tidal web (large-scale, nonlocal), a curvature-based web (more local, peak- and ridge-sensitive), and additional higher-derivative levels that progressively emphasize smaller-scale structure. Because the classification is built from second derivatives of the filtered field, successive hierarchy levels align naturally with operator families that appear in renormalised bias and effective descriptions of large-scale structure, providing an explicit bridge between cosmic-web environments and long- and short-range nonlocal bias ingredients. We quantify the information content of the hierarchy with a compact statistic: we map each cell to one of four ordered web types (void, sheet, filament, knot), construct a corresponding ``web contrast'' field, and measure its cross-correlation with halos from the AbacusSummit simulation suite on a coarse mesh with $\Delta L\simeq 5.5\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$. We find that the hierarchy retains significant tracer-relevant information from very large scales down to the mesh Nyquist limit, with the more local (curvature/higher-derivative) levels dominating toward nonlinear scales. This makes the spectral hierarchy a practical, interpretable conditioning basis for fast mock-galaxy production and field-level modelling, and a flexible tool for studying environment-dependent clustering and assembly bias.

papers.authors: Sayan Saha, Jacqueline E. McCleary, Spencer W. Everett, Maya Amit, Georgios N. Vassilakis, Emaad Paracha, Leo W.H. Fung, Steven J. Benton, William C. Jones, Gavin Leroy, Eric M. Redmond, Jason D. Rhodes, Andrew Robertson, L. Javier Romualdez, Jurgen Schmoll, Ellen Sirks, Sut Ieng Tam, André Z. Vitorelli, Alfredo Zenteno
papers.abstract: We present the weak gravitational lensing dataset from the Super-pressure Balloon-Borne Imaging Telescope (SuperBIT), which imaged 30 galaxy clusters during its 45 night flight in April to May 2023. SuperBIT is a first-of-its-kind balloon-borne imaging telescope that achieved near diffraction-limited observations in near-space conditions above 98% of the Earth's atmosphere. We use the metacalibration algorithm to obtain calibrated galaxy shapes for our target clusters and several calibration fields, enabling unbiased reconstruction of the weak-lensing signal. We employ several diagnostics throughout the pipeline, including assessments of point-spread function (PSF) modeling residuals and their impact on weak-lensing measurements, as well as tests for correlations between galaxy shapes and measured galaxy and PSF properties. To assess the multiplicative shear bias of the pipeline, we analyze a parallel set of simulated images that incorporate the real observing conditions from the flight, including measured SuperBIT PSFs, observed sky backgrounds, and detector noise, yielding a bias of $(1.54 \pm 6.00)$ per cent.

papers.title: Estimates of the Dynamic Characteristics of Binary Systems for Traversable Wormholes Search
papers.authors: I. A. Moiseev, O. S. Sazhina
papers.abstract: The paper presents simulated detectability of traversable wormholes (WHs) in wide binary astrophysical systems without accretion (dormant binary systems) and in the Galactic center. The wormhole spacetime is represented as a gluing of two asymptotically flat Schwarzschild spacetimes, without specifying the detailed geometry of the throat. The gravitational perturbation across the throat is calculated by matching the monopole perturbations on the two sides in the short-throat approximation. We consider a traversable WH candidate as a compact object in a binary system, whose companion star is perturbed by a massive object on an elliptical orbit on the other side of the WH throat. In the case of a supermassive BH as WH candidate the perturbing acceleration is analyzed and compared with the stochastic gravitational influence of surrounding stars. For dormant wide binary systems, we analyze the radial velocity perturbations and discuss how their signatures may differ from those of a triple system. We discuss the observational limits of our model arising due to the Keplerian orbit subtraction. Under the model assumptions and the considered observational sampling, radial velocity perturbations are detectable in simulations with an observational accuracy of 1.5 km/s for all considered observation time spans. For a more conservative accuracy of 5 km/s, the non-parametric analysis method becomes statistically significant after $\approx17$ years of simulated data accumulation. The spectral and non-parametric methods significantly reduce the required accumulation time compared to matched-filtering applied in isolation.

papers.title: Cosmological discrete self-similarity in primordial black hole formation
papers.authors: Luis E. Padilla, Tomohiro Harada, Ethan Milligan, David Mulryne
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that discrete self-similarity (DSS), originally discovered in the asymptotically flat collapse of a massless scalar field, survives in primordial black hole (PBH) formation within an expanding cosmological background. Using fully relativistic simulations of massless scalar-field collapse in a Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker universe, we resolve the near-critical regime and find clear log-periodic oscillations in the PBH mass-scaling relation. This result provides a proof of principle that PBHs may retain information about the critical behaviour in their formation realized in the early Universe: PBH formation in scalar-field kination exhibits DSS, while radiation-fluid collapse is characterized by continuous self-similarity. The resulting mass scaling imprints characteristic log-periodic modulations in an illustrative PBH mass spectrum, which may survive when PBH formation is dominated by a sufficiently narrow range of scales, with possible consequences for PBH phenomenology. Our results show that PBHs may encode not only the amplitude of primordial perturbations, but also the nature of the matter sector and the dynamical state of the Universe at horizon re-entry.
